# `Q-13-5` — Sidebar `auto:` Ignored

> A sidebar `auto:` entry was ignored because the document is
> being rendered without a project index.

## What this means

Sidebars support an `auto:` shorthand: instead of listing every
document by hand, the entry says "include every renderable
document under this directory" and Quarto expands it against
the project's index at render time. This warning fires when an
`auto:` entry is encountered but no project index is available
— typically because the document is being rendered standalone,
not as part of a project build.

The render still succeeds; the `auto:` entry simply expands to
nothing.

## Why this happens

Most often: rendering a single file
(`quarto render report.qmd`) that has been authored as part of
a project. The
file's sidebar configuration is processed, but standalone
renders do not build a project index, so `auto:` has nothing
to expand against.

## How to fix

Render the document as part of a project build (`quarto render`
with no arguments, from inside the project root). If you do
want to render a single file standalone with the sidebar
present, replace the `auto:` entry with an explicit list of
documents.
